extracted.intended_audience: affected domestic producers (and anyone alleging eligibility), associations representing producers, successors, and their legal/financial advisors seeking CDSOA distributions
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for submitting certifications to U.S. Customs and Border Protection to claim distributions under the Continued Dumping and Subsidy Offset Act (CDSOA) for listed antidumping/countervailing duty orders or findings. Covers content, timing, documentation, verification, and payment/recoupment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission / 60-day deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifications to obtain a continued dumping and subsidy offset under a particular order or finding must be received by CBP no later than 60 calendar days after the date of publication of this notice of intent to distribute in the Federal Register. All certifications not received by the 60th day will not be eligible to receive a distribution and will be summarily denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Certifications must be received by July 27, 2021 for this notice. Failure to file within the 60-day window makes the claimant ineligible regardless of whether they appeared on the USITC list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification content required (per 19 CFR 159.63(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 19 CFR 159.63(b), the certification must contain: (1) The date of this Federal Register notice; (2) The Department of Commerce antidumping or countervailing duty case number; (3) The case name (product/country); (4) The name of the domestic producer and any name qualifier; (5) The mailing address of the domestic producer (physical street address if PO box); (6) The IRS number (with suffix), employer identification number, or social security number; (7) The specific business organization (corporation, partnership, sole proprietorship); (8) The name(s) of contact person(s) with phone, mailing address, facsimile, and email; (9) The total dollar amount claimed; (10) The dollar amount claimed by category; (11) A statement of eligibility; and (12) For non-electronic submissions, an original signature by an individual legally authorized to bind the producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All items must be provided. For non-electronic submissions, original signatures are required. The certification must enumerate qualifying expenditures and demonstrate eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification format and submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no required format for a certification, but CBP has developed a standard certification form (CBP Form Number 7401, “Continued Dumping and Subsidy Offset Act of 2000 Certification”) available at https://www.pay.gov. The form can be submitted electronically through pay.gov or by mail. All certifications not submitted electronically must include original signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing address for mailed certifications: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Revenue Division, Attention: CDSOA Team, 6650 Telecom Drive, Suite 100, Indianapolis, IN 46278. CBP will publish a list of certifications received on the CBP website shortly after the receipt deadline; that list only confirms receipt, not acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying expenditures — categories and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying expenditures eligible for offset are those incurred by the domestic producer after issuance of an antidumping or countervailing duty order or finding (including expenditures incurred on the date of the order's issuance), and prior to its termination, provided they fall within certain categories. Categories include: (1) Manufacturing facilities; (2) Equipment; (3) Research and development; (4) Personnel training; (5) Acquisition of technology; (6) Health care benefits for employees paid by the employer; (7) Pension benefits for employees paid by the employer; (8) Environmental equipment, training, or technology; (9) Acquisition of raw materials and other inputs; (10) Working capital or other funds needed to maintain production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-revoked orders/findings, expenditures must have been incurred before October 1, 2007 (due to CDSOA repeal language); for revoked orders, expenditures must be incurred before the effective date of revocation. Expenditures must be related to production of the same product that is the subject of the order or finding (associations are limited to expenditures they themselves incurred in connection with a specific case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount claimed — calculation and prior distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification must indicate: (1) The total amount of any qualifying expenditures previously certified by the domestic producer, and the amount certified by category; (2) The total amount of those expenditures which have been the subject of any prior distribution for the order or finding; and (3) The net amount for new and remaining qualifying expenditures being claimed in the current certification (previous total minus prior distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with 19 CFR 159.63(b)(2)(i)-(iii), CBP will deduct the amount of any prior distribution from the producer's claimed amount for that case. Any false statements about amounts may give rise to liability under the False Claims Act and/or criminal prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to receive distribution / affected domestic producer definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'affected domestic producer' means any manufacturer, producer, farmer, rancher or worker representative (including associations) who: (A) Was a petitioner or interested party in support of a petition with respect to which an antidumping duty order, a finding under the Antidumping Act of 1921, or a countervailing duty order has been entered; (B) Remains in operation continuing to produce the product covered by the order or finding; and (C) Has not been acquired by another company or business that is related to a company that opposed the antidumping or countervailing duty investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must include a statement of eligibility and must state whether the domestic producer remains in operation and continues to produce the product and whether it has been acquired by an opposing or related company; if the producer is no longer operating or producing the covered product, it will not be considered an affected domestic producer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor company and purchaser liability
rubrics_metrics.description: A successor to a company that was an affected domestic producer at the time of acquisition will be deemed to have consented to joint and several liability for the return of any overpayments arising under 19 CFR 159.64(b)(3) that were previously paid to the predecessor. CBP may require the successor to provide documents to support eligibility. Any individual or company who purchases any portion of the operating assets of an affected domestic producer (or its successor or prior recipient) may be jointly and severally liable for the return of overpayments, regardless of whether the purchaser is deemed a successor for purposes of receiving distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successor claimants should consult 19 CFR 159.61(b)(1)(i) and be prepared to provide supporting documentation; filing as a successor carries possible repayment obligations for prior overpayments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association filings and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If an association does not file on behalf of members, the association must provide its members with a statement that contains notarized company-specific information including dates of membership and an original signature from an authorized representative. An association filing on behalf of a member must provide a power of attorney or other evidence of legal authorization from each domestic producer it represents. An association filing on behalf of a member is responsible for verifying the legal sufficiency and accuracy of the member's financial records and is jointly and severally liable with the member for repayment of any claim found to have been paid or overpaid in error. An association may file a certification in its own right, but qualifying expenditures are limited to those the association itself incurred after the date of the order or finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certifications under 19 CFR 159.61(b)(1)(ii), the claimant must name the association, establish membership at the time the association filed the petition, and establish current membership. Associations acting for members must maintain authorization documentation and verify members' supporting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and correction of certification
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP may, at its sole discretion, subject timely certifications to review before acceptance to ensure that informational requirements are complied with and that amounts appear correct. A certification found to be materially incorrect or incomplete will be returned to the domestic producer within 15 business days after the close of the 60-calendar-day filing period. CBP must receive a corrected certification within 10 business days from the date of the original denial letter. Failure to receive a corrected certification within 10 business days will result in denial of the certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will not speculate as to the reason for the error (e.g., intentional vs typographical). It is the claimant's sole responsibility to ensure correctness; failure to do so can result in denial and/or demand for return of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of certifications and records retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifications are subject to CBP verification. The burden is on each claimant to fully substantiate all elements of its certification. Parties are required to maintain, and be prepared to produce, records adequately supporting their claims for a period of five years after the filing of the certification. Records must demonstrate that each qualifying expenditure was actually incurred and support how expenditures are related to production of the product covered by the order or finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CBP later seeks verification and sufficient supporting documentation is not provided as determined by CBP, amounts paid are recoverable as overpayments. Submission of false statements, documents, or records may give rise to liability under the False Claims Act and/or criminal prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of claimant information
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the claimant, the total dollar amount claimed on the certification, and the total dollar amount that CBP actually disburses to that affected domestic producer will be available for disclosure to the public as specified in 19 CFR 159.63(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of the certification is construed as an understanding and acceptance that these items may be disclosed publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution method, timing, and withholding pending legal issues
rubrics_metrics.description: All distributions will be issued by paper check to the address provided by the claimants. CBP intends to include amounts temporarily sequestered during the fiscal year in the distribution and to distribute not later than 60 days after the first day of the subsequent fiscal year in accordance with 19 U.S.C. 1675c(c). CBP may withhold an amount of funds corresponding to a claimant's alleged pro rata share pending resolution of legal issues that could affect eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 159.62(a) provides that CBP will publish a notice of intent to distribute at least 90 calendar days before the end of a fiscal year; failure to meet that publication timing does not affect the claimant's obligation to timely file within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpayments and CBP recovery remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: All overpayments to affected domestic producers are recoverable by CBP. CBP reserves the right to use all available collection tools to recover overpayments, including but not limited to garnishments, court orders, administrative offset, enrollment in the Treasury Offset Program, and/or offset of tax refund payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants are advised to set aside distributed funds because amounts distributed may be subject to recovery due to reliquidations, court actions, administrative errors, or insufficient verification. Negotiation of distribution checks is treated as acknowledgment and acceptance of the obligation to return funds upon demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple certifications using same qualifying expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a domestic producer files a separate certification for more than one order or finding using the same qualifying expenditures as the basis for distribution in each case, each certification must list all the other orders or findings where the producer is claiming the same qualifying expenditures (per 19 CFR 159.63(b)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose other filings that claim the same expenditures could affect eligibility and lead to recovery of overpayments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of list of certifications received does not equal acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of all certifications received will be published on the CBP website shortly after the receipt deadline. This publication will not confirm acceptance or validity of the certification, but merely receipt of the certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to high volume, CBP is unable to respond to individual telephone or written inquiries regarding the status of a certification appearing on the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for duties derived from NAFTA-origin goods
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP does not list cases related to NAFTA on the Preliminary Amounts Available report, and no distributions will be issued on cases where duties were derived from goods from countries that are parties to the North American Free Trade Agreement, per the Federal Circuit's ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers should not expect distributions for NAFTA-derived duties and should not file claims for such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole responsibility and potential liabilities for incorrect certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: It remains the sole responsibility of the domestic producer to ensure that the certification is correct, complete, and accurate so as to demonstrate eligibility for the distribution requested. Any false statements made in connection with certifications may give rise to liability under the False Claims Act and/or criminal prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP may withhold funds pending legal issues; incorrect or incomplete certifications may be denied or returned for correction and could lead to demands for repayment.
